cards.front: friction
cards.back: A force that acts when two surfaces rub together. It slows things down or stops them.
cards.say: friction. A force that acts when two surfaces rub together. It slows things down or stops them.

cards.front: In which direction does friction act?
cards.back: Opposite to the direction the object is moving or trying to move.
cards.say: In which direction does friction act? Opposite to the direction the object is moving or trying to move.

cards.front: air resistance
cards.back: A kind of friction. Air pushes against things moving through it and slows them down.
cards.say: air resistance. A kind of friction. Air pushes against things moving through it and slows them down.

cards.front: water resistance
cards.back: A kind of friction. Water pushes against things moving through it and slows them down.
cards.say: water resistance. A kind of friction. Water pushes against things moving through it and slows them down.

cards.front: streamlined
cards.back: Having a smooth, pointed shape that lets air or water flow past easily, so there is less resistance.
cards.say: streamlined. Having a smooth, pointed shape that lets air or water flow past easily, so there is less resistance.

cards.front: Why are fish and dolphins streamlined?
cards.back: Their smooth, pointed bodies reduce water resistance, so they can swim fast.
cards.say: Why are fish and dolphins streamlined? Their smooth, pointed bodies reduce water resistance, so they can swim fast.

cards.front: How does a parachute slow a person down?
cards.back: Its large canopy catches a lot of air, so air resistance is big.
cards.say: How does a parachute slow a person down? Its large canopy catches a lot of air, so air resistance is big.

cards.front: What does friction often produce?
cards.back: Heat. Rub your hands together quickly and they get warm.
cards.say: What does friction often produce? Heat. Rub your hands together quickly and they get warm.

cards.front: lubricant
cards.back: A slippery substance, such as oil, that reduces friction between moving parts.
cards.say: lubricant. A slippery substance, such as oil, that reduces friction between moving parts.

cards.front: Why do we oil a bicycle chain?
cards.back: The oil reduces friction between the moving parts, so the chain moves easily and wears less.
cards.say: Why do we oil a bicycle chain? The oil reduces friction between the moving parts, so the chain moves easily and wears less.

cards.front: Which surface has more friction, rough or smooth?
cards.back: Rough. Its bumps catch on the other surface.
cards.say: Which surface has more friction, rough or smooth? Rough. Its bumps catch on the other surface.

cards.front: Which gives more friction for a shoe: carpet or ice?
cards.back: Carpet. Ice is very smooth and slippery.
cards.say: Which gives more friction for a shoe: carpet or ice? Carpet. Ice is very smooth and slippery.

cards.front: Why do trainers have grooves on the soles?
cards.back: The grooves give grip, which means more friction with the ground.
cards.say: Why do trainers have grooves on the soles? The grooves give grip, which means more friction with the ground.

cards.front: How do bicycle brakes stop the wheel?
cards.back: The brake pads rub on the wheel. The friction slows the wheel down.
cards.say: How do bicycle brakes stop the wheel? The brake pads rub on the wheel. The friction slows the wheel down.

cards.front: Give an example of useful friction.
cards.back: Walking without slipping, gripping a pencil, or brakes stopping a car.
cards.say: Give an example of useful friction. Walking without slipping, gripping a pencil, or brakes stopping a car.

cards.front: Why can friction be a problem?
cards.back: It wears out moving parts and wastes energy as heat in machines.
cards.say: Why can friction be a problem? It wears out moving parts and wastes energy as heat in machines.

cards.front: Which falls more slowly: a flat sheet of paper or a crumpled ball of paper?
cards.back: The flat sheet. It has a bigger surface to push against the air, so air resistance is larger.
cards.say: Which falls more slowly: a flat sheet of paper or a crumpled ball of paper? The flat sheet. It has a bigger surface to push against the air, so air resistance is larger.

cards.front: How does a bigger surface area affect air resistance?
cards.back: A bigger surface area facing the air makes air resistance bigger.
cards.say: How does a bigger surface area affect air resistance? A bigger surface area facing the air makes air resistance bigger.

cards.front: Why do racing cyclists crouch low?
cards.back: It makes their bodies smaller to the air, so there is less air resistance.
cards.say: Why do racing cyclists crouch low? It makes their bodies smaller to the air, so there is less air resistance.

cards.front: Why do swimmers wear tight swimming caps?
cards.back: A smooth, tight cap makes the swimmer more streamlined, so there is less water resistance.
cards.say: Why do swimmers wear tight swimming caps? A smooth, tight cap makes the swimmer more streamlined, so there is less water resistance.

cards.front: How can you measure the friction on an object?
cards.back: Pull it along a surface with a forcemeter. The reading in newtons shows the friction force.
cards.say: How can you measure the friction on an object? Pull it along a surface with a forcemeter. The reading in newtons shows the friction force.

cards.front: Is friction a contact force?
cards.back: Yes. Friction only acts when two surfaces touch.
cards.say: Is friction a contact force? Yes. Friction only acts when two surfaces touch.

cards.front: Why does a spacecraft keep moving in space without engines running?
cards.back: There is almost no air in space, so there is almost no air resistance to slow it down.
cards.say: Why does a spacecraft keep moving in space without engines running? There is almost no air in space, so there is almost no air resistance to slow it down.
